items.stem: The Family Medical Leave Act, the first bill President Bill Clinton’s administration signed into law in February 1993, guarantees eligible employees what?
items.stemEs: La Ley de Licencia Médica Familiar, el primer proyecto de ley que la administración del presidente Bill Clinton convirtió en ley en febrero de 1993, garantiza a los empleados que cumplen los requisitos ¿qué?

choices.text: Up to twelve weeks of paid leave each year for the birth of a child or a serious illness in the family
choices.textEs: Hasta doce semanas de licencia remunerada cada año por el nacimiento de un hijo o una enfermedad grave en la familia
choices.explanation: The duration and the reasons are right and the pay is not. The act requires that the job be held open, and no federal law requires an employer to pay for that leave — which is the limit most often missed and the reason later state laws were written.
choices.misconception: reads the everyday sense of leave as paid time off rather than the law's terms

choices.text: Up to twelve weeks of unpaid, job-protected leave each year for specified family and medical reasons
choices.textEs: Hasta doce semanas al año de licencia no remunerada con protección del empleo por motivos familiares y médicos determinados

choices.text: Continued health insurance coverage for workers during the period between one job and the next
choices.textEs: Cobertura de seguro de salud continuada para los trabajadores durante el periodo entre un empleo y el siguiente
choices.explanation: That protection exists and comes from two other laws — the continuation coverage of 1985 known as COBRA, and the portability provisions of the 1996 health insurance act. This act is about time away from a job a worker keeps.
choices.misconception: answers with the laws covering the gap between jobs rather than leave within one

choices.text: Twelve weeks of leave from employers of every size, including the smallest businesses
choices.textEs: Doce semanas de licencia en empresas de todo tamaño, incluidas las más pequeñas
choices.explanation: The entitlement is real and its reach is narrower: the act covers employers with fifty or more employees, and an employee must also have worked a qualifying period. A substantial share of the workforce is outside it.
choices.misconception: treats a statute with an employer-size threshold as covering every workplace

items.dokRationale: Recall of what one statute provides. The student retrieves the terms of a law; no reasoning about how a coalition formed or a process worked is involved. A DOK 2 item on this standard requires that reasoning.
items.explanation: The two features that define the act are the ones most often mis-stated: the leave is UNPAID, and what the law actually protects is the job rather than the income. Earlier versions had passed Congress twice and been vetoed, which is why a bill of this kind was ready to sign in the administration's first month.
items.explanationEs: Las dos características que definen la ley son las que más a menudo se enuncian mal: la licencia es NO REMUNERADA, y lo que la ley protege realmente es el puesto y no el ingreso. Versiones anteriores habían pasado por el Congreso dos veces y habían sido vetadas, y por eso un proyecto de este tipo estaba listo para firmarse en el primer mes de la administración.

items.stem: The House of Representatives approved the North American Free Trade Agreement in November 1993 by 234 votes to 200, with most Democrats against it and most Republicans for it, while President Bill Clinton’s administration pressed hard for passage. What does that vote show about the politics of trade in the period?
items.stemEs: La Cámara de Representantes aprobó el Tratado de Libre Comercio de América del Norte en noviembre de 1993 por 234 votos contra 200, con la mayoría de los demócratas en contra y la mayoría de los republicanos a favor, mientras la administración del presidente Bill Clinton presionaba con fuerza para que se aprobara. ¿Qué muestra esa votación sobre la política comercial del periodo?

choices.text: Trade agreements must be ratified by a two-thirds vote of the Senate, which is why support from the other party was necessary to reach the threshold
choices.textEs: Los acuerdos comerciales deben ser ratificados por dos tercios del Senado, y por eso el apoyo del otro partido era necesario para alcanzar ese umbral
choices.explanation: Treaties need two thirds of the Senate; this was not submitted as a treaty. It was approved as a congressional-executive agreement, by simple majorities of both houses, which is how most modern trade agreements have been handled.
choices.misconception: applies the Senate's treaty threshold to an agreement approved by ordinary majorities

choices.text: Organized labour supported the agreement because it opened Mexican markets to goods made in American factories
choices.textEs: Los sindicatos apoyaron el tratado porque abría los mercados mexicanos a bienes fabricados en fábricas estadounidenses
choices.explanation: The direction is reversed. The labour federation campaigned against the agreement and lobbied Democratic members to vote no, on the argument that manufacturing work would move south rather than that exports would move north.
choices.misconception: inverts organized labour's position on the agreement

choices.text: Trade divided each party internally rather than dividing one party from the other, so a president carried it with the other party's votes
choices.textEs: El comercio dividió internamente a cada partido en lugar de separar a un partido del otro, de modo que un presidente lo sacó adelante con los votos del otro partido

choices.text: The agreement had been negotiated and signed by the previous administration, so the vote was a formality that merely recorded a settled decision
choices.textEs: El tratado había sido negociado y firmado por la administración anterior, de modo que la votación era un trámite que solo registraba una decisión ya tomada
choices.explanation: The first half is correct: it was negotiated under President George H. W. Bush and signed in December 1992, and side agreements on labour and the environment were added afterward. It was no formality — 234 to 200 after a public campaign on both sides is among the closest major trade votes of the century.
choices.misconception: treats a contested ratifying vote as a formality because the text predated it

items.dokRationale: The student must read a roll-call division and infer what it says about where the disagreement lay. Recalling that NAFTA took effect in 1994 is the DOK 1 version of this content.
items.explanation: Trade split both parties internally rather than separating them from each other. A Democratic president carried the agreement with mostly Republican votes and against the opposition of organized labour, which had been among his party's core supporters — which is why the fight was conducted inside each party's caucus rather than between them.
items.explanationEs: El comercio dividió internamente a los dos partidos en lugar de separarlos entre sí. Un presidente demócrata sacó adelante el tratado con votos mayoritariamente republicanos y contra la oposición de los sindicatos, que habían estado entre los apoyos centrales de su partido; por eso la pelea se libró dentro de cada bancada y no entre ellas.

items.stem: The House impeached President Bill Clinton’s in December 1998 and the Senate acquitted him in February 1999, with neither article reaching 67 votes. What does the pairing of those two outcomes show about the constitutional process?
items.stemEs: La Cámara acusó al presidente Bill Clinton en diciembre de 1998 y el Senado lo absolvió en febrero de 1999, sin que ninguno de los dos artículos alcanzara 67 votos. ¿Qué muestra la combinación de esos dos resultados sobre el proceso constitucional?

choices.text: Impeachment is a charge brought by the House, and removal requires a separate two-thirds vote of the Senate that neither article received
choices.textEs: La acusación es un cargo presentado por la Cámara, y la destitución exige una votación aparte de dos tercios del Senado que ninguno de los dos artículos obtuvo

choices.text: Impeachment removes a president from office, and the Senate's acquittal restored him to the presidency
choices.textEs: La acusación destituye a un presidente del cargo, y la absolución del Senado lo restituyó en la presidencia
choices.explanation: This is the single commonest misunderstanding of the clause. Impeachment is the accusation and nothing more; he remained president throughout, performed the duties of the office and delivered a State of the Union address between the two votes.
choices.misconception: reads impeachment as removal rather than as the charge that precedes a trial

choices.text: A president acquitted by the Senate cannot afterward be charged in an ordinary court for the same conduct
choices.textEs: Un presidente absuelto por el Senado no puede ser acusado después en un tribunal ordinario por la misma conducta
choices.explanation: The Constitution says the opposite in the same breath as it describes the judgement: a party convicted or acquitted in an impeachment remains liable to indictment and trial according to law. The Senate's verdict is about holding office, not about guilt in a criminal sense.
choices.misconception: carries the criminal rule against double jeopardy into an impeachment judgement

choices.text: He was the first president in American history to be impeached, so the Senate had no precedent of any kind to guide the conduct of its trial
choices.textEs: Fue el primer presidente en la historia estadounidense en ser acusado, de modo que el Senado no tenía precedente de ningún tipo que guiara la conducción del juicio
choices.explanation: He was the second. Andrew Johnson was impeached in 1868 and the Senate fell one vote short of removing him, and the rules and procedures of that trial were consulted directly in 1999.
choices.misconception: treats the better-remembered impeachment as the first one

items.dokRationale: The student must distinguish two stages of one process and explain why opposite outcomes at each are not a contradiction. Recalling the dates of the impeachment and the acquittal is the DOK 1 version of this content.
items.explanation: Impeachment and removal are separate acts by separate chambers. The House brings the charge by simple majority, which is what happened in December; conviction and removal require two thirds of the Senate, which is the 67 votes neither article received. So a president can be impeached and remain in office, and this president did — which is also what happened in 1868.
items.explanationEs: La acusación y la destitución son actos distintos de cámaras distintas. La Cámara presenta el cargo por mayoría simple, que es lo que ocurrió en diciembre; la condena y la destitución exigen dos tercios del Senado, que son los 67 votos que ningún artículo obtuvo. Así que un presidente puede ser acusado y permanecer en el cargo, y este presidente lo hizo, igual que ocurrió en 1868.
